concepts.label: Key-Value Data Operations (get/upsert/insert/replace/remove) via the Collection API
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - `doc upsert`/`UpsertAsync()`/`upsert()` and `doc replace`/`ReplaceAsync()`/`replace()` are the same upsert/replace operations already documented in java-sdk/howtos/kv-operations.md.

concepts.label: CAS (Compare-And-Swap) Optimistic Locking
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - the replace example explicitly fetches the current CAS and passes it to `ReplaceAsync`/`replace()` ('To ensure data has not been modified before executing the replace operation, pass the document's CAS value to the method'), the canonical optimistic-locking pattern already documented on the SDK's kv-operations/concurrent-mutations pages.

concepts.label: Sub-Document Operations (lookupIn/mutateIn - path-level get/upsert/replace/remove within a document)
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - minted once for this batch in reading-data.json; this page's 'Updating a Sub-Document' section (`MutateInAsync`/`mutateIn`/`MutateInSpec.upsert()`) is the same concept, the upsert-shaped instance of it.

relations.subject: sdk:kv-operations
relations.evidence: Use the `ReplaceAsync()` function to update a document in Couchbase. To ensure data has not been modified before executing the replace operation, pass the document's `CAS` value to the method.

relations.subject: sdk:kv-operations
relations.evidence: To change a specific field inside a document, you can perform a Sub-Document operation. You can use either a Sub-Document upsert or replace operation depending on what's required for your application.

notable_absence.finding: No RBAC/privilege mention for upsert/replace, consistent with the rest of the KV-operation guide pages in this batch.

cross_component_finding: This page's KV `upsert`/`replace` share a name with the n1ql UPSERT statement (n1ql:upsert) documented in cloud/guides/insert.md and cloud/n1ql/n1ql-language-reference/upsert.md, but the two are a genuinely different access path (Collection API vs SQL++ statement); this page itself gives no textual evidence of an explicit disjointness statement (unlike java-sdk kv-operations.md's explicit mustUseInsteadWhen framing), so no relation was minted here - flagging as a naming-collision worth watching rather than asserting a relation without a quote. Repeats, verbatim, the same warning banner and related-links lists shared across creating-data.md, deleting-data.md, reading-data.md and bulk-operations.md.
